basic_details.scholarship_name: KTH Royal Institute of Technology Master's Scholarship
basic_details.offering_entity: KTH Royal Institute of Technology (Kungliga Tekniska högskolan)
basic_details.host_institutions_covered: KTH Main Campus & Kista ICT Campus (Stockholm, Sweden)
basic_details.major_restrictions: Master's programmes across all engineering and technology schools, notably School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (EECS): Computer Science, Machine Learning, Cybersecurity, Software Engineering, and Information and Network Engineering.
basic_details.number_of_awards_total: ~10% of admitted fee-paying international students receive tuition waivers (~40 to 60 full tuition fee waivers awarded annually)
basic_details.number_of_awards_pakistan: Open international competition; Pakistani engineering graduates typically secure 3 to 6 tuition waivers annually
basic_details.duration_of_scholarship: 2 years (120 ECTS credits), subject to passing a minimum of 45 ECTS credits during Year 1

nationality_requirements: Citizens of non-EU/EEA/Swiss countries liable to pay tuition fees in Sweden
eligibility_requirements.academic_qualifications: A recognized 4-year Bachelor's degree (16 years education) in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or related STEM discipline from an HEC-recognized university with high academic distinction (minimum cumulative GPA of 3.50 / 4.00 or 80%+ aggregate; top 10% class standing preferred).
eligibility_requirements.grading_conversion_notes: Transcripts are rigorously evaluated on Swedish scale; competitive applicants present high grades in advanced mathematics, algorithms, and systems courses.
eligibility_requirements.subject_background_prerequisites: Substantial coursework in mathematics (calculus, linear algebra, discrete math, probability) and core computing (algorithms, data structures, computer architecture, programming).
eligibility_requirements.current_education_status: Students in their final year of undergraduate studies are eligible to apply conditionally.
eligibility_requirements.work_experience_notes: Not mandatory; leadership, industrial software engineering experience, and technical projects enhance the application profile.
eligibility_requirements.language_notes: IELTS Academic min 6.5 (no section below 5.5) or TOEFL iBT min 90 (written test min 20). Medium of Instruction letters not accepted for degrees from Pakistan (English 6 requirement).
eligibility_requirements.other_language_requirements: None; all Master's programmes at KTH are taught entirely in English.
eligibility_requirements.gender_specific_requirements: None; women in engineering actively encouraged.
eligibility_requirements.special_eligibility_categories: Candidates must rank KTH as their first choice (priority 1) in their Swedish national application on Universityadmissions.se.
eligibility_requirements.previous_scholarship_restrictions: Cannot be combined with Swedish Institute (SI) scholarships or other full tuition waivers.

tuition_fee.details: 100% tuition fee waiver covering full tuition costs for the 2-year Master's degree (SEK 320,000 to SEK 380,000 value; ~USD 30,000 to 36,000).

admission_application_fee.details: Swedish national application fee of SEK 900 paid online via Universityadmissions.se.

accommodation.details: KTH accommodation office assists scholarship holders with student housing guarantees (SSSB / KTH housing); rent in student dorms or corridor rooms averages SEK 4,500 to 7,500/month.

monthly_stipend.details: The KTH Scholarship is a tuition waiver only; living costs (approx. SEK 10,314/month required by Swedish Migration Agency) must be covered through personal funds, family savings, or part-time work.

airfare.details: International flights between Pakistan and Stockholm Arlanda (ARN) are self-funded.

visa_fee.details: Swedish Residence Permit for Higher Education application fee of SEK 1,500 paid online to Migrationsverket.

health_insurance.details: All fee-paying and scholarship students are covered by the Swedish state collective insurance plan (FAS+) covering emergency medical and dental care.

food_allowance.details: Groceries and meals self-funded; student kitchens in dorms allow economical self-cooking (~SEK 2,500/month).

books_and_materials_allowance.details: Free access to electronic course literature via KTH Library, software licenses, and computing laboratories.

research_funding_conference_grant.details: Travel grants available through KTH schools for master's thesis research presented at academic conferences.
research_funding_conference_grant.amount: Up to SEK 10,000 per conference presentation

travel_transit_allowance.details: SL student discount provides discounted monthly travelcards for Stockholm metro, buses, commuter trains, and ferries.
travel_transit_allowance.amount: Student discount on Stockholm SL transit

university_and_program_options.single_or_multiple_universities: Single premier Swedish engineering institution: KTH Royal Institute of Technology (Stockholm, Sweden)
participating_institutions: School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (EECS)
Center for Autonomous Systems & AI at KTH
university_and_program_options.university_rankings_scope: Top 75 global university (QS World #73, QS Subject Computer Science #54, THE World #97); Sweden's largest and most prestigious technical university.
available_majors: Master's Programme in Software Engineering of Distributed Systems
Master's Programme in Information and Network Engineering
Master's Programme in Interactive Media Technology
university_and_program_options.admission_requirements_summary: 4-year BS in CS/STEM with 3.5+ GPA, official transcripts, CV, motivation letter, and IELTS 6.5+ or TOEFL 90+. KTH must be selected as Priority 1.
university_and_program_options.easiest_hardest_institutions_guidance: Machine Learning and Computer Science are the most competitive programmes with the highest GPA cutoffs; Software Engineering of Distributed Systems, Embedded Systems, and Cybersecurity offer slightly more favorable admission ratios.
university_and_program_options.strategic_program_match_advice: You MUST list KTH as your first priority programme on Universityadmissions.se to be eligible for the KTH Scholarship. Scholarship applications for second-priority choices are not reviewed.

application_process_roadmap.portal_system_name: Universityadmissions.se (Swedish National Higher Education Portal) & KTH Scholarship Portal
application_process_roadmap.account_creation_instructions: Create account on Universityadmissions.se, apply for KTH as Priority 1 by mid-January, then submit the dedicated KTH Scholarship application on kth.se in December/January.
step_by_step_workflow: Step 1 (October - January): Apply for KTH Master's programme as Priority 1 on Universityadmissions.se.
Step 2 (By mid-January): Pay the Swedish application fee of SEK 900 online.
Step 3 (Early December - Mid January): Open the dedicated KTH Scholarship application form on kth.se.
Step 4 (In KTH portal): Enter your 8-digit University Admissions application number, upload motivation essay and CV.
Step 5 (By 1 February): Upload all supporting academic documents (transcripts, degree certificates, English test) to Universityadmissions.se.
Step 6 (Late March): Swedish national admission results published on Universityadmissions.se.
Step 7 (Early April): KTH Scholarship recipients officially announced by email.
Step 8 (April - June): Apply for Swedish Residence Permit for Higher Education via Migrationsverket online portal.
application_process_roadmap.university_vs_scholarship_routing: Two-step application: Programme admission applied via Universityadmissions.se; KTH Scholarship applied via separate online form on kth.se.
application_process_roadmap.recommendation_letters_submission_method: Not required for general KTH admissions or scholarship.
application_process_roadmap.personal_statement_prompts: KTH Scholarship Motivation Essay: Max 500 words explaining why you chose KTH, your academic achievements, and how your studies will contribute to sustainable development goals.
application_process_roadmap.cv_format_requirements: 1-2 page academic CV detailing education, programming proficiencies, capstone projects, and distinctions.
application_process_roadmap.interview_format_details: No interviews; selections made purely through academic assessment and motivation essay review.
application_process_roadmap.standardized_tests: IELTS Academic (6.5+) or TOEFL iBT (90+). GRE is NOT required.
application_process_roadmap.attestation_requirements: Certified copies of degree and transcript uploaded to Universityadmissions.se; HEC attestation recommended.
application_process_roadmap.translation_requirements: Certified English translations required for all non-English documents.
application_process_roadmap.final_submission_method: National application on Universityadmissions.se + scholarship form on kth.se.

required_documents_checklist.specification: Scanned color copy of original degree certificate and official English translation.
required_documents_checklist.pakistan_specific_instruction: Pakistani applicants submit 4-year BS degree; HEC attestation recommended.

required_documents_checklist.specification: Complete consolidated semester transcripts detailing all completed course units, grades, and grading scale.
required_documents_checklist.pakistan_specific_instruction: Ensure transcript clearly states credit hours and grading scale (CGPA out of 4.0).

required_documents_checklist.specification: Max 500-word essay explaining academic ambitions, choice of KTH, and alignment with UN Sustainable Development Goals.
required_documents_checklist.pakistan_specific_instruction: Focus on technological challenges in Pakistan/developing world and how KTH engineering will provide solutions.

required_documents_checklist.specification: 1 to 2 page CV detailing academic background, technical skills, projects, and honors.
required_documents_checklist.pakistan_specific_instruction: Highlight final-year project (FYP) and technical tools.

required_documents_checklist.specification: Official IELTS Academic TRF (6.5+) or TOEFL iBT score report (90+) sent to University Admissions in Sweden.
required_documents_checklist.pakistan_specific_instruction: Must satisfy Swedish English 6 requirement; institutional MOI letters are not accepted for Pakistani degrees.

required_documents_checklist.specification: Clear color copy of valid international passport bio-data page.
required_documents_checklist.pakistan_specific_instruction: Ensure passport is valid for at least 2 years beyond intended arrival.

important_dates_timeline.annual_cycle_notes: Single annual intake for autumn semester. KTH must be designated as Priority 1 on Universityadmissions.se.

selection_process_and_weights.academic_weight: 60% (Academic excellence, CGPA, grades in mathematics and core computing coursework)
selection_process_and_weights.personal_statement_weight: 20% (KTH Scholarship essay evaluating motivation and sustainability alignment)
selection_process_and_weights.selection_panel_composition: KTH Central Scholarship Committee and School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science Academic Board.
selection_process_and_weights.evaluation_methodology: Two-tier merit evaluation: Applicants are ranked first by academic performance and grading tier of the home university. High-ranking applicants are then evaluated on their motivation essay and contribution to sustainable development.

competitiveness_profile.total_annual_applicants: 4,500+ fee-paying international applicants across KTH Master's programmes
competitiveness_profile.total_scholarships_awarded: ~40 to 60 full tuition fee waivers awarded annually
competitiveness_profile.acceptance_rate_pakistan: ~1% to 2% among qualified Pakistani STEM applicants
competitiveness_profile.typical_academic_and_research_profile: Undergraduate degree in CS/EE from top Pakistani institution (FAST, NUST, LUMS, GIKI, UET), top 5% of class, compelling sustainability essay, IELTS 7.5+.
competitiveness_profile.common_backgrounds_of_winners: Graduates of NUST, FAST-NUCES, LUMS, and GIKI.
competitiveness_profile.high_representation_countries: China, India, Pakistan, Turkey, United States, Iran, Indonesia

fake_websites_and_scams: Unauthorized overseas education agencies claiming guaranteed admission or scholarships at KTH. Applications are strictly merit-based via Universityadmissions.se and kth.se.
red_flags_and_warnings.application_fee_warning: Swedish national application fee of SEK 900 paid only via Universityadmissions.se. KTH scholarship application itself is free.
red_flags_and_warnings.agent_and_intermediary_warnings: KTH does not work with recruitment agents. Plagiarized or AI-generated motivation essays are disqualified immediately.
hidden_costs_breakdown: Swedish Residence Permit application fee: SEK 1,500 (~PKR 39,000).
Living cost proof required by Swedish Migration Agency: SEK 10,314 / month (~PKR 268,000 / month; SEK 103,140 for 10-month bank statement = ~PKR 2,680,000).
Flight ticket from Pakistan to Stockholm: ~PKR 250,000 to 380,000.
misleading_claims_debunked: CLAIM: The KTH Scholarship covers living expenses. (FACT: The KTH Scholarship covers 100% of tuition only; living costs must be self-funded).
CLAIM: You can apply for the scholarship with KTH as your second priority. (FACT: KTH must be your Priority 1 choice on Universityadmissions.se).
official_vs_unofficial_discrepancies: Third-party websites confuse the KTH Scholarship with the Swedish Institute (SI) Scholarship. The SI Scholarship covers living stipends, while the KTH Scholarship is tuition-only.

scholarship_obligations_and_terms.minimum_gpa_maintenance: Must pass at least 45 ECTS credits during the first academic year to retain the tuition waiver for Year 2.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.attendance_requirements: Full-time physical enrollment on campus in Stockholm.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.academic_progress_monitoring: Annual credit completion check by KTH Scholarships Office before renewing the waiver.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.work_restrictions_during_study: Swedish residence permit allows international students to work without hourly limits, provided satisfactory academic progress is maintained.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.home_country_return_obligation: None. International graduates qualify for a 1-year residence permit to seek employment or start a business in Sweden.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.repayment_clawback_conditions: No clawback of previously waived tuition; failure to achieve 45 ECTS results in loss of waiver for Year 2.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.rules_for_changing_major: Changing programme requires formal application during the next admission cycle.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.extension_policy: Scholarship is granted for the nominal 2-year duration (120 ECTS) and cannot be extended.
